newsitem.title: USA: Stepan sees improved surfactant earnings.
newsitem.headline: Stepan sees improved surfactant earnings.

text.p: Stepan Co said surfactant earnings improvement should lead the way to record company earnings in 1997.
"Polymer earnings grew significantly during the fourth quarter," said president Quinn Stepan, "but were overshadowed by weaker surfactant earnings."
Surfactant earnings for 1996 were down "mostly due to weak profit margins from competitive pressures throughout North America and Europe."

Stepan shares were unchanged at 19 Thursday after the company reported net earnings for 1996 rose 18 percent to $19 million, or $1.80 per share, compared to $16.1 million, or $1.51 per share, in 1995. Net sales were $536.6 million, up two percent from $528.2 million.

Record 1996 polymer earnings were attributed to increased polyurethane polyol volume and improved profit margins, while phthalic anhydride earnings declined on slightly lower volume and margins. Polyurethane systems reported higher earnings resulting from increased volumes and improved margins, said the chemicals manufacturer.

"The impact of German start-up losses, unusually high domestic maintenance expenditures, and competitive pressure on pricing, negatively affected surfactant earnings. Fortunately, operating expenses declined by $8.7 million pre-tax as a result of lower legal and environmental costs," Stepan said.

Legal and environmental costs in 1996 benefited from insurance recoveries as compared to significant charges recorded in the prior year. The 1996 provision for income taxes rose due to higher foreign tax provisions, it said.
